minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 6, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on June
6, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 3, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

PUBLIC COMMENTS

There were no comments from members of the audience.

NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  1  June 6, 2011
 1.  City Council Consideration of Acquiring a Leasehold Interest in the O’Neill
  Elementary School Pursuant to the Naylor Act Offer Made by the Saddleback
  Valley Unified School District

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and described the City’s rights, under
  the Naylor Act, to lease the surplus school property under the recreation/public use
  definition. The City Council has 60 days to decide whether they wish to advise the
  District that the City has a lease-hold interest in the school property.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to
  consider, in Closed Session, the matter of a potential leasehold agreement with the
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District for O’Neill Elementary School.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8. Real property Denoted as Assessor’s Parcel No. 784-291-01
  with a Common Street Address of 24701 San Doval, Mission Viejo, California,
  Commonly Known as O’Neill Elementary School Owned by Saddleback Valley
  Unified School District The Negotiating Parties are: City of Mission Viejo; Dennis
  Wilberg, City Manager, Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson,
  Director of Community Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney.
  Owner Negotiators are: Saddleback Valley Unified School District, Clint Harwick,
  Superintendent. Under Negotiation will be the Price and Terms of a Lease-Hold
  Interest in the Real Property. (Only if City Council approves and directs negotiation
  in the prior Open Session Item).

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  2  June 6, 2011
 At the hour of 5:17 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for CS1, the City Council directed staff to investigate
negotiations with the Saddleback Valley Unified School District on the O’Neill school property.
For item CS2, the Council provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adoptable Pets of the Month

  Mayor Leckness highlighted three animals available for adoption at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Services Center.

P2.  Recognize Waste Management for their $4,268.55 Donation to the Friends of the
  Mission Viejo Library

  Mayor Leckness received the donation and presented a certificate of appreciation to
  Michelle Clark of Waste Management.

P3.  Recognize the Mission Viejo High School Diablos Varsity Baseball Team for Their
  Championship Win at the Division 2 CIF Finals at Dodgers Stadium on Thursday,
  June 2, 2011

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of recognition to the Diablos baseball team
  members and coaches.

P4.  Recognize "What the Constitution Means To Me" Essay Winners

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of recognition to the following essay contest
  winners: 9-12 grade category – 2nd place winner, Timothy M. Aney from Capistrano
  Valley Christian School and 1st place winner, Sonia L. Zhang from Capistrano Valley
  Christian School; 7-8 grade category – 3rd place winner, Shannon Elizabeth Howell from
  Heritage Christian School, 2nd place winner, Seth M. Thompson from Heritage Christian
  School and 1st place winner, Courtney Clark from Heritage Christian School. The
  Teacher of the Year awards were presented to Margie Haney from Capistrano Valley
  Christian School and Emily Updegraff from Heritage Christian School. Those unable to
  attend were Courtland M. Sherreitt from Capistrano Valley Christian School, 3rd place

City Council Minutes  3  June 6, 2011
   winner in the 9-12 grade category and Allison Oetken from Pioneer Middle School, 3rd
  place winner in the 7-8 grade category.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Carole Weidler, M.V.: thanked the City for providing a memorable and well-planned Memorial
Day ceremony and stated that Mission Viejo honors the fallen with dignity, with grace, and with
honor.

Steve Bell, San Clemente: speaking as a volunteer for the American Cancer Society, he thanked
the City Council for their continued commitment to the Relay for Life.

Chuck Costello and Jerry Corpuz, M.V.: announced that the name of the Saddleback Valley
YMCA has been changed to the Mission Viejo Family YMCA to reflect that the majority of
members are from Mission Viejo.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed his thanks to the City Council Members for their efforts in
keeping Mission Viejo financially stable. He also asked the Council to support the establishment
of an OCFA pension reform committee.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: discussed the Relay for Life efforts and thanked Steve Bell, Ashley
Blair, Barbara Swanson and Denise Matson. She stated that the event was very well-run and she
was so impressed by the three City Council Members who attended and the number of staff that
volunteered their time.

Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that the 17th Annual DAWG Walk will be held on Saturday, June
18, 2011. Interested parties can register on the DAWG web site at www.dawg.org.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 8, 10, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 20 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  June 6, 2011
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes from the regular City Council Meeting of May 16, 2011, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated May 6, 2011, in the amount of $736,896.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated May 13, 2011, in the amount of $545,559.48

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated May 20, 2011, in the amount of $1,435,458.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Pension Reform Ordinance

  Adopted Ordinance 11-289 Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract Between the
City  Council of the City of Mission Viejo and the Board of Administration of the California
  Public Employees' Retirement System.

7.  Senior Appointee Vacancy on the Community Services Commission

  Received the letter of resignation from Community Services Commissioner Senior
  Appointee John Maginnis, and directed the City Clerk to schedule appointment of a new
  member for the City Council Meeting of June 20, 2011.

9.  Annual Routine Fleet Vehicle Maintenance Services

  (1) Awarded a contract to Mission Viejo Services Center, Inc. (A11-41) for Annual
  Routine Fleet Vehicle Services for the period of July 1, 2011 to June 30, 2013 in an
  amount not to exceed $106,200.00; and (2) authorized the issuance of a purchase order to

City Council Minutes  5  June 6, 2011
   Mission Viejo Services Center, Inc. for the period July 1, 2011 to June 30, 2012, in
  amount not to exceed $53,100.00, pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2011-2013 budget
  by the City Council.

11.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2011 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-35 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt
  on Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City
  Council to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for
  Hearing Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to
  Destroy Weeds in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3)
  instructed the City Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 15, 2011.

12.  Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  (1) Approved County Agreement D11-004 with the County of Orange (A11-43) for the
  period July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $1,975,224.00; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1,
  2011, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $987,612.00, pending adoption
  of the 2011-13 Budget by the City Council.

13.  Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791):  Temporary
  Construction Easements

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to purchase the Temporary Construction Easements
  (TCEs) from the Mission Viejo Country Club (MVCC) required for the widening of Oso
  Parkway from I-5 to Country Club Drive for $50,185 utilizing CDA funds; and (2)
  authorized the City Clerk to record the easement deeds in the office of the County
  Recorder subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and City Engineer.

16.  Annual Support for Integrated Library System Software and Hardware for the
  Mission Viejo Library

  Approved payment of Annual Support for Integrated Library System Software and
  Hardware for the Mission Viejo Library for FY 2011-12 to SirsiDynix in the amount of
  $33,537.05.

19.  Designation of Positions Authorized to Apply for Disaster Assistance

  Adopted Resolution 11-36 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents for the

City Council Minutes  6  June 6, 2011
   Purpose of Obtaining Federal Financial Disaster Assistance and/or State Financial
  Disaster Assistance.

21.  Third Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Services Outsourcing
  Agreement

  Approved the Third Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Services
  Outsourcing Agreement with Baker and Taylor, Inc., (A09-13C) and issue a purchase
  order in an amount not to exceed $100,000 for the total term of the two-year Agreement
  pending approval of the 2011-2013 budget by the City Council.

22.  Annual Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services

  (1) Rejected all bids received for the Annual Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting,
  and Sealing Services; and (2) approved the Seventh Amendment (A07-43G) to the
  subject contract extending the contract two months and to increase the contract in the
  amount of $8,000.

*Item 33 was taken out of order.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Schlicht

33.  Repair Pool Decking at the Marguerite Tennis and Swim Center

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  The following spoke in support of the recommended action: Coach Bill Rose, Mission
  Viejo Nadadores, M.V.; Julie Nassif, M.V.; Susan Shoults, M.V.; Laura Dobbs, M.V.;
  Chloe Sutton, M.V.; and Wendy Bucknum, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, that for the
  preservation of the public health, safety and welfare, Council directs staff to return within
  90 days with a process to begin the completion of the city’s contractual obligation, so that
  at the conclusion of the 2012 Summer Olympics, the city can repair the pool decking of
  the city owned swimming facility leased to the Mission Viejo Nadadores Foundation.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  June 6, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

23.  Development Code Amendment DCA2011-15, Being a Proposed Ordinance
  Amending Section 9.29.220 to Title 9 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Pertaining to Subdivision Sales and Model Home Directional Signs

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Jeff Smith, Lennar Homes: stated that the banners that Lennar installed on Los Alisos
  have increased the flow of traffic and helped with their home sales.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance No. 11-290 Amending Section 9.29.220 to Title 9 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Pertaining to Subdivision Sales and Model Home Directional Signs

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

24.  Service Cost Recovery Study

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 11-37 Establishing New Fees for Recreation and Tennis Centers.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  8  June 6, 2011
 NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

25.  City Council Communication with Auditors

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Bryan Gruber, Lance, Soll & Lunghard, LLP, Brea: presented an outline of the audit
  process and invited the City Council Members to contact his office if they have any
  questions throughout the audit.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive correspondence from Lance, Soll & Lunghard, LLP, the City’s independent
  auditors, regarding the upcoming financial statement audit for the fiscal year ending June
  30, 2011, and determine that the City is in agreement with the planned scope and timing
  of the audit.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

26.  Draft Orange County Sustainable Communities Strategy

  Gail Shiomoto-Lohr, GSL Associates, La Canada-Flintridge: presented an overview of
  the draft Orange County Sustainable Communities Strategy.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and Repair

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the wording in the agenda report matches a prior
  agenda report however there is a quarter million dollar reduction in this contract.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the contract amount is
  determined by the proposed budget and is for standardized, as-needed services.

City Council Minutes  9  June 6, 2011
   Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill clarified that the bid estimates are
  comprised of a list of hourly rates with an estimated quantity for standard skilled trades
  such as carpentry and masonry. Those items are added up for a bid total and the contract
  is actually budget-driven.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) award
  a contract for the subject services to Jamey Clark, Inc. (A11-40) for the period of July 1,
  2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $ 676,000.00; and (2) authorized issuance
  of a purchase order to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011, through June 30,
  2012, in an amount not to exceed $ 338,000.00 pending adoption of the 2011-2013
  budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

10.  Playground, Parkland, and Facilities Safety Inspection Services

  Council Member Schlicht asked why the bid amount is different from the proposed
  contract amount. She noted that there is a $42,000 increase this year, compared to the
  prior year, yet the contractor is the same.

  Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill responded that the bids are monthly
  inspection figures. He does not know why the contractor’s bid was $42,000 higher than
  last year's figure however it may have something to do with the incredible amount of
  liability and indemnification that the contractor provides the City.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) award
  a contract for the subject services to Jamey Clark, Inc. (A11-42) for the period of July 1,
  2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $ 282,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance
  of a purchase order to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011, through June 30,
  2012, in an amount not to exceed $ 141,000.00 pending adoption of the 2011-2013
  budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht

City Council Minutes  10  June 6, 2011
   ABSENT: None

14.  Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  Council Member Reardon asked the Director of Public Works to outline her recent
  questions about cosmetic cracks and slurry seal repair.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon described a photograph that Council Member
  Reardon had shared with him and stated that the integrity of the slurry material is still
  there. He noted that the crack pictured in the photograph was typical of separation that
  occurs from expansion and contraction and it is a cosmetic issue only. He further
  described that there are a few areas that staff has scheduled for repair where there are
  significant or wider cracks. He noted that slurry seal is a maintenance application
  intended to extend the life of the pavement underneath.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she feels slurry sealing is a waste of money if cracks
  are appearing as quickly as they are. She also expressed concern with the award of a
  contract to American Asphalt since they are responsible for problems on Olympiad Road.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) certify the
  completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City
  Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the
  Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance
  and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and
  (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

15.  Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Council Member Reardon stated that she asked her question during discussion of the
  previous agenda item.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)

City Council Minutes  11  June 6, 2011
   authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

17.  Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program - Housing
  Rehabilitation Consulting Services

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht thanked staff for finding a way to reduce the costs for this
  contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  an Agreement with Housing Rehabilitation Consulting Services (A11-44) from July 1,
  2011 to June 30, 2013, in an amount not to exceed $109,000 ($54,500 /year) for
  Technical Assistance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

18.  Youth Services Program Contract

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Members questions.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is not in favor of the City taking over the youth
  services program.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)

City Council Minutes  12  June 6, 2011
   approve the Fifth Amendment to the Contract with the Saddleback Valley Unified School
  District (SVUSD) Department of Recreation and Community Services (A03-103E) to
  provide Youth Services Programs through Fiscal Year 2011-12 in the amount of
  $712,000; and (2) direct staff to develop a plan to transition the management and
  administration of the Youth Services Program to the City’s Recreation and Community
  Services Department

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

20.  FY 2011-12 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Council Member Schlicht thanked Lt. Mike Gavin for his service to the community and
  she inquired about the Sheriff’s Department on-line services.

  Lt. Gavin responded that staff has to review the blotter to ensure that confidential
  information isn’t released before the blotter is made public. He is currently trying to fill a
  vacant position and hopes that blotter items will be released faster in the near future. He
  also addressed Council Member Schlicht’s question about crime stats and said he would
  find out why the stats are no longer posted on line. He concluded his comments by
  informing the Council that the School Resource Officer (SRO) program is very effective
  but he doesn't expect that other cities will agree to share in the cost of the program.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  approved the FY 2011-12 Law Enforcement Services Agreement (A11-45) with the
  County of Orange for an amount not to exceed $15,169,689; and (2) authorize the City
  Manager to approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount
  not to exceed $65,000 for FY 2011-12.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

City Council Minutes  13  June 6, 2011
 27.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

  Steven Wontrobsky, M.V.: stated that OCFA has a major shortfall due to under-reporting
  in the past and he asked Council Member Kelley to resign from the OCFA Board to
  eliminate any appearance of a conflict of interest.

28.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.

29.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing new to report.

30.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

31.  Proposed 2011-13 Budget for the City of Mission Viejo

  City Manager Wilberg presented an outline of the proposed 2011-13 budget

  By consensus, the City Council Members set the date for a budget workshop on June 15,
  2011, at 6:00 p.m.

City Manager Wilberg announced that he has selected Cheryl Dyas, the current finance director
for the City of Laguna Niguel, as the replacement for Director of Administrative Services Irwin
Bornstein who is retiring. Mr. Wilberg also announced that he has appointed Keith Rattay to
assume the Assistant City Manager duties.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  14  June 6, 2011
 32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Relay for Life and announced that she
signed up to participate in the Cancer Prevention Study (CPS-3.) Information obtained in the
study will provide research to help fight cancer and she stated that it is an honor for her to
participate. She also announced that her relay team, Kelley’s Heroes, won the award for the
most laps run. She thanked the four Marines on her team who ran twenty miles each. Council
Member Kelley reminded residents that the DAWG Walk will be held on Saturday, June 18,
2011. She also congratulated Director of Public Services Keith Rattay who will be stepping up
to be the Assistant City Manager when Mr. Bornstein retires. Mr. Rattay is a very competent,
talented person and she knows he will do a great job. Council Member Kelley announced that
the Community of Character word for the month of June is citizenship and the character movie,
John Adams - Part I, will be shown on June 26 in the City Council Chamber.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at recent events including a tour of the
community center, a meeting with a resident and a tennis center employee during which a
conflict was resolved, the ACCOC Housing Summit and Infrastructure Conference, the
Government Leaders Prayer Breakfast, and the Capo High School orchestra performance. She
noted that the City’s Memorial Day service was extremely significant to her and she was pleased
to meet the families of some of the fallen heroes featured on the American Heroes banners. She
also attended the Relay for Life and she thanked City staff for their hard work. Council Member
Reardon discussed the May 16 City Council Meeting and stated that residents have shared their
concern that the salary and pension reform discussion was cut short. She wishes she had asked
the Mayor to continue the discussion instead of ending the conversation there. Lastly, Council
Member Reardon stated that perception is reality. Some individuals have accused the City
Manager of creating a list of cost saving measures to buttress his position on a staff salary
increase. She stated that the accusations are not true and the City Manager provided the list at
her request.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she too heard a lot of comments about the salary and
pension discussion. She stated that transparency is not something that always happens here.

City Council Minutes  15  June 6, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht invited residents and business owners to view a web site created by
Mission Viejo citizens with the intent to sustain, retain, and gain businesses in Mission Viejo
(www.missionviejobusiness.com.) She announced that she too attended the Memorial Day
ceremony and she noted that it was a very solemn, emotional observance and tribute to our fallen
heroes. She also attended an open house for California Youth Services, a nonprofit organization
that helps families in crisis. She encouraged those who have drug or alcohol problems to admit it
and ask for help via California Youth Services or Teen Challenge. Council Member Schlicht
asked the Mayor to dedicate this meeting to the 9,000 who died or were wounded on D-Day,
June 6, 1944.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that the Council hears the same platitudes about transparency over
and over again. He thanked his colleagues for indulging his wish to leave the last meeting early
so he could attend his daughter’s high school awards ceremony however; he heard the opposite
comments from constituents about the salary and pension discussion. He stated that the feedback
he received was that certain Council Members had just one goal to run out the clock since he had
to leave early. Mayor Pro Tem Ury noted that he tries to take a very consistent stand and he
finds if very interesting when Council Members vote one way in closed session and another way
in open session. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Ury encouraged his colleagues to ask questions of staff
prior to the budget meeting on June 15.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness reiterated Mayor Pro Tem Ury’s comments about the salary and pension
discussions at the last meeting. He allowed each Council Member to speak once and at a certain
point, he felt that Council Member Schlicht was repeating what she had already said. He called
for the vote at that time. Mayor Leckness discussed his attendance at the Relay for Life and his
participation in the Cancer Prevention Study. He also discussed his attendance at the Mission
Viejo High School Diablos baseball game at Dodgers stadium, the Memorial Day Ceremony, the
Disneyland Scholarship presentation where two Capo High School students were awarded
scholarships. Mayor Leckness announced that the Pacific Symphony will be held on July 30,
2011, and he encouraged residents to attend. Lastly, he announced that the Mission Viejo
